# Outcome sub-dossier — Samson Resources Corporation realized record after the August 2015 restructuring, ~3-5-year horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the registrant terminated its (voluntary)
> SEC reporting immediately after the reported event, there is no post-event public 10-K;
> the realized record is traced through the deregistration filing, the company's own
> press release, and reputable press. This sub-dossier contains no information about how
> the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the event (feasibility-relevant)
- On August 17, 2015 — three days after the reported agreement — the Company filed a Form 15-15D certifying termination of its voluntary filing of reports under Sections 13 and 15(d) of the Exchange Act, relying on Rule 15d-6; the form states the Company "is a voluntary filer and is not subject to the filing requirements of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934." [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-15-292733, Form 15-15D]
- The Form 15-15D reports approximately 45 holders of record of the covered 9.750% Senior Notes due 2020 and states the Company would continue reporting only to its noteholders and credit-facility lenders through a password-protected website. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-15-292733, Form 15-15D]
- No annual report (Form 10-K) or other periodic report was filed by the Company after August 2015; consequently no audited public financial statements exist for the ~2018-2020 outcome window, and the realized-record facts below rely on the deregistration filing, the company's press release, and reputable press rather than on later primary SEC financial statements. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-15-292733, Form 15-15D]

## Realized trajectory — the Chapter 11 case
- In September 2015 Samson Resources Company and eight affiliates filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware. [SRC: https://www.coleschotz.com/new-delaware-chapter-11-filing-samson-resources-company-et-al/]
- The reorganization did not proceed uncontested: on approximately September 27, 2016 the bankruptcy judge refused the debtors' request to extend their exclusivity period, allowing the official unsecured creditors committee to file a competing reorganization plan; Judge Sontchi stated "I think this is a situation where the debtor is using exclusivity as a sword" and found "the debtors have not engaged constructively or even in good faith with the official committee." [SRC: https://www.forbes.com/sites/debtwire/2016/09/27/samson-resources-bankruptcy-judge-wont-extend-exclusivity-opening-door-for-competing-creditor-plan/]
- The unsecured creditors committee argued the debtor refused to negotiate a plan and sought to pursue fraudulent-transfer and lien-challenge claims; the debtor's own proposal at that stage would have paid first lien lenders (owed approximately $950 million) in full, with partial reduction from asset sales and refinancing of the remainder into a revolving loan facility. [SRC: https://www.forbes.com/sites/debtwire/2016/09/27/samson-resources-bankruptcy-judge-wont-extend-exclusivity-opening-door-for-competing-creditor-plan/]

## Realized trajectory — confirmation and emergence
- The U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware confirmed the plan of reorganization on February 13, 2017, and the company emerged from Chapter 11 on March 1, 2017. [SRC: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/samson-resources-emerges-from-bankruptcy-300416368.html]
- Under the plan, substantially all of Samson Resources Corp.'s remaining assets, including its subsidiaries, were transferred to a newly formed entity, Samson Resources II, LLC; the majority of the equity in Samson II was distributed to Samson Resources Corp.'s second lien lenders, both on account of their bankruptcy claims and in connection with a $60 million rights offering. [SRC: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/samson-resources-emerges-from-bankruptcy-300416368.html] [SRC: https://www.ogj.com/general-interest/article/17288064/samson-resources-emerges-from-bankruptcy-sheds-4-billion-in-debt]
- The reorganization discharged approximately $4 billion of debt and nearly $300 million of annual interest expense; post-emergence debt financing consisted of a first lien revolving credit facility with an initial borrowing base of $280 million, of which $245 million was outstanding on the effective date, leaving greater than $60 million in total liquidity. [SRC: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/samson-resources-emerges-from-bankruptcy-300416368.html] [SRC: https://www.ogj.com/general-interest/article/17288064/samson-resources-emerges-from-bankruptcy-sheds-4-billion-in-debt]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable
- Reputable press reported total debt of approximately $4.2 billion (including approximately $2.25 billion owed to unsecured noteholders) as of the Chapter 11 filing, but this filing-date scalar is not traceable in this build to a retrieved primary SEC financial statement (the registrant had ceased public reporting) and is recorded here as [UNVERIFIED]. [UNVERIFIED]
- The exact petition date reported by some press as September 16, 2015 was not confirmed against a retrieved primary court document in this build; the reported event's contemplated outside petition date was September 16, 2015. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- After agreeing to the restructuring in August 2015 and immediately terminating its voluntary SEC reporting, the registrant carried out the contemplated chapter 11 restructuring: it filed for Chapter 11 in Delaware in September 2015, passed through a contested plan process (loss of exclusivity in 2016 and a competing creditor plan), and had a plan confirmed on February 13, 2017 with emergence on March 1, 2017 — the going-concern oil-and-gas business surviving intact but with its equity transferred to a new holding entity (Samson Resources II, LLC) owned chiefly by the former second lien lenders after roughly $4 billion of debt was discharged. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-15-292733, Form 15-15D] [SRC: https://www.forbes.com/sites/debtwire/2016/09/27/samson-resources-bankruptcy-judge-wont-extend-exclusivity-opening-door-for-competing-creditor-plan/] [SRC: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/samson-resources-emerges-from-bankruptcy-300416368.html]

[SLICE END]
